scenes.tts: When is a synapse finished? When it is there, when it releases, or when the other side responds?
scenes.visual: Title card: There, but Not Working. A single excitatory synapse drawn simply, with three unlit lamps beneath it labelled There, Releases, Responds.
scenes.narration: When is a synapse finished? When it is there, when it releases, or when the other side responds?

scenes.tts: A mature muscle fiber is usually contacted by one motor axon, at one site, using one transmitter.
scenes.visual: A muscle fiber with one endplate and one motor axon; label: one axon, one site, acetylcholine.
scenes.narration: A mature muscle fiber is usually contacted by one motor axon, at one site, using one transmitter.

scenes.tts: A neuron in the brain receives thousands of synapses. Excitatory and inhibitory synapses share one dendrite, so each contact must specify its kind.
scenes.visual: A cortical pyramidal neuron; one dendrite zooms in to show glutamate synapses and GABA synapses side by side, each with its own receptors.
scenes.narration: A neuron in the brain receives thousands of synapses. Excitatory and inhibitory synapses share one dendrite, so each contact must specify its kind.

scenes.tts: A finished synapse does three things. It is there. It releases transmitter. And the other side responds.
scenes.visual: Back to the single synapse; the three lamps light one by one: There, Releases, Responds.
scenes.narration: A finished synapse does three things. It is there. It releases transmitter. And the other side responds.

scenes.tts: They can come apart, and each needs its own measurement.
scenes.visual: The three lamps separate slightly; each gets a small icon beneath it.
scenes.narration: They can come apart, and each needs its own measurement.

scenes.tts: A microscope shows it is there. A dye taken up by recycling vesicles shows release. A recording shows the response.
scenes.visual: Icons under the lamps: electron microscope under There, a glowing dye spot under Releases, a recording pipette and current trace under Responds.
scenes.narration: A microscope shows it is there. A dye taken up by recycling vesicles shows release. A recording shows the response.

scenes.tts: Take stargazer, a mouse that tosses its head upward and has seizures.
scenes.visual: A schematic mouse tilting its head upward. Label: stargazer, a spontaneous mutant.
scenes.narration: Take stargazer, a mouse that tosses its head upward and has seizures.

scenes.tts: In its cerebellum, granule cells receive synapses from mossy fibers.
scenes.visual: Cerebellum outline; a mossy fiber terminal contacts a small granule cell.
scenes.narration: In its cerebellum, granule cells receive synapses from mossy fibers.

scenes.tts: AMPA receptors carry most fast excitatory current.
scenes.visual: The granule cell synapse enlarged: two receptor types under the terminal, labelled AMPA receptor and NMDA receptor.
scenes.narration: AMPA receptors carry most fast excitatory current.

scenes.tts: N M D A receptors open when glutamate and a co-agonist are bound. Near rest, magnesium from outside blocks most of their current.
scenes.caption: NMDA receptors open when glutamate and a co-agonist are bound. Near rest, magnesium from outside blocks most of their current.
scenes.visual: The NMDA receptor with a magnesium ion in its pore and only a small current near rest; when a depolarization arrow appears, the magnesium leaves and the current grows. Label: voltage-dependent block.
scenes.narration: NMDA receptors open when glutamate and a co-agonist are bound. Near rest, magnesium from outside blocks most of their current.

scenes.tts: In stargazer, these synapses give N M D A responses but no AMPA responses. Predict: which property failed?
scenes.caption: In stargazer, these synapses give NMDA responses but no AMPA responses. Predict: which property failed?
scenes.visual: Question card over the synapse with the three lamps: There? Releases? Responds?
scenes.narration: In stargazer, these synapses give NMDA responses but no AMPA responses. Predict: which property failed?

scenes.tts: Not being there. The synapses are present.
scenes.narration: Not being there. The synapses are present.

scenes.tts: Not release either. An N M D A response needs glutamate, so transmitter is being released.
scenes.caption: Not release either. An NMDA response needs glutamate, so transmitter is being released.
scenes.visual: A vesicle releases glutamate; the NMDA receptor lights after depolarization. The Releases lamp lights.
scenes.narration: Not release either. An NMDA response needs glutamate, so transmitter is being released.

scenes.tts: What failed is one kind of response. The same synapse responds through one receptor and not the other.
scenes.visual: The Responds lamp splits in two: NMDA lit, AMPA dark. The AMPA receptor slot is mostly empty.
scenes.narration: What failed is one kind of response. The same synapse responds through one receptor and not the other.

scenes.tts: The gene encodes stargazin, a small membrane protein. It brings AMPA receptors to the cell surface.
scenes.visual: A stargazin protein escorts an AMPA receptor up to the membrane. Credit: Bredt and Nicoll laboratories, 2000.
scenes.narration: The gene encodes stargazin, a small membrane protein. It brings AMPA receptors to the cell surface.

scenes.tts: Its tail binds P S D ninety-five, a scaffold under the synapse, and that holds the receptors there.
scenes.caption: Its tail binds PSD-95, a scaffold under the synapse, and that holds the receptors there.
scenes.visual: Stargazin's tail clips into PSD-95 beneath the membrane; label PSD-95, scaffold.
scenes.narration: Its tail binds PSD-95, a scaffold under the synapse, and that holds the receptors there.

scenes.tts: A count would miss this defect. A recording shows it, and so does labeling the receptors.
scenes.visual: The microscope icon shows a normal-looking synapse; the recording trace shows NMDA current only; a receptor-label panel shows little AMPA receptor at the synapse.
scenes.narration: A count would miss this defect. A recording shows it, and so does labeling the receptors.

scenes.tts: So carry one idea through this lesson. A synapse that is there is not yet a synapse that works.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: A synapse that is there is not yet a synapse that works.
scenes.narration: So carry one idea through this lesson. A synapse that is there is not yet a synapse that works.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: each experiment sees only the properties it measures.
scenes.visual: Closing card: three lamps, three measurements.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: each experiment sees only the properties it measures.
